label: rem:blowup-topological-selection
title: Topological selection rule on the blowup obstruction
html:
Remark. Topological selection rule on the blowup obstruction

The descent condition and vortex reconnection. The twisted 2-cocycle condition

  d(g_{ijk}^{(n)}) = a_{ij}^{(n)} \cdot g_{ijk}^{(n)}
  \cdot (a_{jk}^{(n)})^{-1}

fails at the singular set \Sigma because the transition functions g_{ij}^{(n)} develop discontinuities there. These discontinuities correspond to vortex reconnection events where the divisor topology changes. The obstruction class \kappa_{n^*} measures the total topological change at \Sigma. It acts as the net "reconnection charge": the signed count of reconnection events weighted by their fusion-rule multiplicities.

Constraint from Berry phase. The obstruction class must align with \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation theory. The class \kappa_{n^*} must lie in the image of the character map:

  \chi \colon
  \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2))
   \to 
  H^2(\Sigma, \mathcal{B}).

This restricts the possible values of \kappa_{n^*} to a discrete lattice. This forms a topological selection rule on the blowup. We permit only vorticity concentrations with cohomological charges compatible with the categorical structure.
